The Protecting Medical Research Funding Act (H.R. 2855) explicitly blocks impoundment or reprogramming of NIH funds without congressional approval. Ron Patterson’s situation highlights why this matters—medical research saves lives.

But the real issue isn’t funding levels, it’s bureaucratic bloat. The NIH’s $47B budget includes $1.8B for facility costs and $6B for indirect expenses like administrative overhead. While cancer trials stall, 30% of grant money gets diverted to university bureaucracy instead of labs.

We need accountability, not blank checks. Prioritize patients over paperwork—slash redundant compliance layers and redirect every dollar to frontline research.
